_comment.about: base/nextjs is the shared kernel (ADR-005): unlike domain SDKs whose installable content root is templates/, its content root is src/ (mirroring base/dart/lib/src). Next.js has no package mechanism, so kernel modules reach hosts by file copy: installs points at src/services directly and lands the whole kernel services surface at app/services/base/, imported by hosts and by other SDKs' copied files as '@/app/services/base/...'. Since 1.2.0 it also carries the paas-era shell chrome (sidebar, navs, dashboard/admin home, layout) and the admin settings/CMS surfaces as flat templates/ entries in the one top-level installs list (no app_type persona blocks; admin and manager see similar pages and the page code hides what the other role should not see). Since 1.3.0 the kernel's platform-gateway.ts also carries the tenant/session wrapper the paas-era shell kept in app/lib/paas-gateway.ts (paasCall): the tenant base URL is resolved per request (session site, request host, env) and the session's API credentials go out as the Authorization header, mirroring the Dart kernel's HttpService + TokenInterceptor. Since 1.4.0 it also carries the generic landing hero (components/custom/hero.tsx) with its copy in components/custom/landing/hero-config.ts and the section registry components/custom/landing/hero-sections.ts: a feature SDK contributes a section under the hero input by injecting one line at the registry's // @rokct-sdk-hero-sections-start marker through its manifest integrations (the same contract as the nav and compose-flag markers), and the hero loads registered sections with a dynamic import, so the hero itself stays free of any feature's code. Since 1.5.0 the rest of the landing HOST is generic too - and only the host: app/landing/page.tsx (reads the session through the kernel seam and prefetches the platform's plans via app/actions/base/landing.ts), the client orchestrator components/custom/landing-content.tsx, the section registry components/custom/landing/page-sections.ts and the generic values in components/custom/landing/landing-config.ts (auth URLs, the nav's hero/footer ends, the plans query - no product copy). Ray, 2026-09-03: each home SDK holds its own landing page, the way a Dart home SDK holds its profile screens. So the content sections of a product's landing page live in that product's home SDK, which registers each one with one line at the // @rokct-sdk-page-sections-start marker, `{ id: "<file>", load: () => import("@/components/custom/<file>") }`; the orchestrator loads them by dynamic import, renders them in ascending meta.order (hero 0, negative before the hero as overlays) and hands each PageSectionProps (id, urls, session, plans, nav). agent_sdk 1.4.0 registers rokctapp's floating nav, logos, chat, social, features, workflow, pricing, comparison, faq and testimonials sections; a shell with nothing registered renders the hero alone. The host files land on the shell's own paths, so the composer overwrites the shell copies. Since 1.6.0 the hero's copy has a seam too: components/custom/landing/hero-copy.ts is a third one-marker registry, // @rokct-sdk-hero-copy-start, where a home SDK registers a module whose default export is a HeroCopy (any subset of HeroConfig: headlineWords, headlineSuffix, wordIntervalMs, placeholders, logoPlaceholderToken, backgroundImage, trustLine, badges, fallbackHref) with one line, `{ id: \"<sdk>-hero\", load: () => import(\"@/components/custom/landing/<file>\") }`; the hero lays it over HERO_CONFIG (hero-config.ts keeps rokctapp's words as the default) and shows no copy while the module loads. Nothing registered renders HERO_CONFIG from the first paint as before, so rokctapp is unchanged; a thin shell such as supacharge gets its own hero words from its home SDK (lms_sdk) instead of editing an installed file that the next compose regenerates. Since 1.7.0 the hero carries no input at all. Ray, 2026-09-08: "no hero work same way as landing, they need to be injected like generic profile, chat box is for chat related stuff, i think if agent sdk is home it inject that chat" - so the search-style input, its typewriter placeholders, the submit and the hero-sections results that sat inside hero.tsx moved out to agent_sdk 1.5.0 (components/custom/landing/agent-hero-form.tsx), and in their place the hero renders the FIRST entry of a fourth one-marker registry, components/custom/landing/hero-form.ts (// @rokct-sdk-hero-form-start, `{ id: "<sdk>-<form>", load: () => import("@/components/custom/landing/<file>") }`), through a next/dynamic loader so the form is server-rendered with the hero; the module's default export takes HeroFormProps (hero, signupUrl, onFocusChange, onActiveChange, onHeadlineWordsChange). hero-sections.ts stays here (feature SDKs still register sections into it) but the registered form, not the hero, consumes it. Nothing registered renders no form: headline, trust line and badges alone (supacharge until lms_sdk registers its own); rokctapp with agent_sdk 1.5.0 renders the same DOM as before. Since 1.8.0 it also carries the platform scrollbar (Ray, 2026-09-08: "rokctai_frontend has a unique scroll with yellow color i think each sdk should use it, so it can move to base sdk"): app/styles/rokct-scroll.css is rokctai_frontend's Custom Scrollbar block (app/globals.css lines 165-189: 6px webkit scrollbar, transparent track, #facc15 thumb, #eab308 on hover, same in .dark) with the values as CSS variables on :root (--rokct-scroll-width, --rokct-scroll-track, --rokct-scroll-thumb, --rokct-scroll-thumb-hover; the yellow is the default, a home SDK rethemes by redefining them). app/landing/page.tsx imports it, so every composed shell has the scroll on /landing with no host edit; a host that wants it on every route adds `@import "./styles/rokct-scroll.css";` to its app/globals.css. rokctai_frontend keeps its own identical rules, so it renders the same. Since 1.9.0 the plans query has a seam too: components/custom/landing/plans-query.ts is a fifth one-marker registry, // @rokct-sdk-plans-query-start, where a home SDK registers a module whose default export is a LandingPlansQuery ({cmd, payload}) or null, with one line, `{ id: "<sdk>-plans", load: () => import("@/components/custom/landing/<file>") }`; app/actions/base/landing.ts prefetches with loadLandingPlansQuery(), which answers the FIRST entry that loads and falls back to LANDING_CONFIG.plansQuery when nothing is registered, so rokctapp still reads the platform Subscription Plan catalog byte-for-byte as before. It exists because that catalog is the plans on which someone RUNS a rokct app (USD 20/200 tenant plans) - right for rokctai_frontend, wrong for a product whose landing sells to its own end users: supacharge's visitors are learners, and lms_sdk registers the tenant's own learner catalog here.
_comment.app/actions/merchants/shop.ts: commerce/merchants (installed by merchants_sdk; the commerce consolidation PR moved app/actions/paas/shop.ts there)
_comment.app/config/features.ts: host shell (feature toggles; hero-config.ts reads them for the store badges)
_comment.app/lib/session.ts: host shell session seam (neutral no-session copy in the bare shell; auth_sdk overwrites it with the NextAuth-backed one). The kernel's session.ts reads the session ONLY through this seam, never through app/(auth).
_comment.components/custom/brand-logo.tsx: host shell (brand mark the hero renders)
_comment.components/custom/branding.tsx: host shell (brand wordmark the hero renders)
_comment.components/custom/header.tsx: host shell (site header the landing host renders; also used by the shell's status and careers pages)
_comment.components/custom/nav/delivery-nav.tsx: delivery repo (no SDK home in paas-map; stays in the shell until the delivery frontend takes it)
_comment.components/custom/nav/merchant-nav.tsx: commerce/merchants (mapped there in paas-map; installed by that SDK)
_comment.components/custom/session-provider.tsx: host shell; auth_sdk 1.4.0 (Users#93) installs it. app-sidebar.tsx and nav/team-switcher.tsx read useSession() from next-auth/react, which only works under the provider this file mounts, so a shell composing base_sdk WITHOUT auth_sdk must ship a pass-through session-provider.tsx (and the next-auth dependency declared above) or /manager 500s
